title: U.S. House · Florida's 11th District
area: Central Florida, including parts of Orange and Lake counties north and west of Orlando.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Daniel Webster did not make the Republican primary ballot. James Pericola won the Democratic primary with 46.3% against Royal Webster and Dan Williams. Joe Strada won a five-way Republican primary with 33.5%, narrowly ahead of Carey Baker (33.0%). Ralph Groves advanced from the Libertarian primary without appearing on the ballot.

summary.text: James Pericola is the Democratic nominee for the open Florida 11th Congressional District seat. An attorney raised in Central Florida, he began as a staffer for Sen. Bob Graham, served in the Clinton administration and later worked as a government affairs executive, according to his campaign website. He says he moved home to care for his aging mother and is running on lowering costs, protecting Social Security, Medicare and healthcare, and democracy issues.

background.text: Says he was raised in Central Florida in a working-class family and is the first in his family to attend college and law school; he graduated from Spruce Creek High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1997) and a law degree (2005) from the Catholic University of America.

Began his career working for U.S. Sen. Bob Graham of Florida as a special assistant, traveling the state with him, according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; his campaign website describes the role as staff assistant.
Served in the Clinton administration as a presidential appointee, Special Assistant to the Chairman of the National Transportation Safety Board, according to his campaign website.

Describes more than 30 years in public service as a congressional staff member, attorney and senior government affairs executive who advised companies, local governments, labor organizations, trade associations and nonprofits.
Says he moved home to Central Florida to care for his aging mother, an experience he cites as shaping his focus on healthcare costs.
Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for Florida's 11th District with 46.3% of the vote, defeating Royal Webster and Dan Williams.
According to his campaign website, he is a husband and father.

priorities.text: Affordability: proposes middle-class tax breaks, federal funding to address the housing crisis and lower property-insurance costs, and holding corporations accountable for price gouging.
Protecting Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid: pledges to reverse Medicaid cuts he says Congress passed and to oppose benefit reductions or privatization, while lowering prescription drug costs.
Protecting democracy: says he would work to pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, oppose "unfair mid-decade redistricting," and restore congressional oversight of the executive branch.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to reverse Medicaid cuts and protect Social Security and Medicare from benefit reductions or privatization, and work to lower prescription drug costs.

summary.text: Joe Strada is the Republican nominee for the open Florida 11th Congressional District seat. According to his campaign website, he started in the skilled trades and grew a family-owned Central Florida company, Strada Services, and he describes himself as not a career politician. He describes himself as a business owner running on immigration enforcement, government accountability, term limits and workforce training.

background.text: Graduated from Lyman High School, according to Ballotpedia; his campaign website says he took a job as a handyman at a bowling alley while still in high school.

According to his campaign website, he entered the skilled trades and grew Strada Services from one van into a family-owned company serving communities across the country, which he says created thousands of jobs.

Says he invested in paid training programs so employees could learn a trade while earning pay, which is why workforce development, apprenticeships and career and technical education are central to his campaign.
Describes himself as a businessman and not a career politician; Ballotpedia lists his profession as business.
Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary for Florida's 11th District with 33.5% of the vote, ahead of Carey Baker (33.0%), Tim Wilkins, Nizam Razack and Ivette Palomo.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife raised their family in Central Florida, and he is a father and grandfather.

priorities.text: Immigration enforcement: says law enforcement needs more resources to address the effects of illegal immigration on public safety and the economy.
Government accountability: says he would work to "root out bureaucrats and policies that enrich greedy politicians and fraudulent NGOs."
priorities.quote: NO ONE SHOULD GET RICH IN PUBLIC OFFICE.

priorities.text: Addressing skilled-worker shortages, citing a training program he developed at his company in response to labor shortages.

positions.summary: Says Florida law enforcement needs more resources to address the effects of illegal immigration on public safety, the economy and infrastructure, and credits President Trump with closing the border.

summary.text: Ralph Groves is the Libertarian Party candidate for Florida's 11th Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army major and Iraq War veteran, he worked as a civilian Defense Intelligence Agency analyst from 1999 to 2018 and is a former chairman of the Libertarian Party of Orange County. His campaign website says he is running on an anti-war platform, protecting Medicare and Social Security, and gun ownership.

background.text: Served on active duty in the Army in the United States and Germany, with Military Intelligence Group-Europe in Heidelberg, before civilian service as a Defense Department analyst.
Earned a Doctor of Arts degree in history from St. John's University, according to his campaign website.

Worked from 1999 to 2018 as a civilian analyst for the Defense Intelligence Agency, covering West African countries from RAF Molesworth, England, (1999-2015) and Iran from DIA headquarters in Washington, including a year at the Pentagon (2015-2018).

Served in the Army Reserve as a detachment commander with the 209th Army Liaison Team, mobilized for the Iraq War in 2008-2009 on the staff of General Petraeus in Baghdad, and retired from the Army as a major in 2010.

Has written books and scholarly articles on Iran, Afghanistan and Cote d'Ivoire, including Soviet Raison d'etat and Relations with Iran's Communist Parties, 1920-1979 and Iran's Shi'ite Clerics' Opposition to the Shah, 1959-1979.
Is a former chairman of the Libertarian Party of Orange County and, according to his campaign website, active with the American Legion and the Southeastern Food Bank.
Resides in Ocoee, Florida; his campaign website says he is married and has five children and three grandchildren.

priorities.text: Opposes U.S. involvement in foreign conflicts, including calling for an immediate cease-fire and mediated peace talks in Ukraine while European allies do more to counter Russia.
Favors simplified, reasonable processes for legal immigration while opposing illegal and unregulated migration.
Would uphold Social Security and Medicare while calling for reduced federal taxes.

positions.summary: Describes himself as pro-life and opposes government funding for abortion providers, but says that in limited cases abortion should be decided by women and their doctors, not government.
positions.quote: In extreme cases, abortion should be decided by women and their doctors, not government.

positions.summary: Opposes new restrictions on gun ownership, including expanded background checks, and supports upholding gun rights under the 2nd Amendment.
positions.quote: Expanded background checks will not keep guns out of the hands of criminals and gang members; in any case, such checks will be inexact as not all records about people are available to adjudicators.

positions.summary: Calls for reducing federal taxes generally rather than raising them, arguing lower taxes will stimulate the economy.
positions.quote: will call for reduction of Federal taxes to stimulate the economy

positions.summary: Supports increasing fossil fuel output and says a transition to renewable energy will take decades, rather than favoring a faster shift away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: Transition to “green energy” will take decades to accomplish.

positions.summary: Supports abolishing the federal Department of Education and giving parents options including vouchers and homeschooling.
positions.quote: a broad range of options should be available to parents, including a voucher system and homeschooling

researchNotes: Open seat (incumbent Daniel Webster did not make the primary ballot). No public record found for Libertarian nominee Ralph Groves beyond his ballot status. Biographies of all three candidates rest largely on their own campaign sites and Ballotpedia; birthplaces and birth years were not found for any of them, and Joe Strada's college education, if any, is not listed.
